gates.reason: Checked corpus and response path containment, symlink-safe task reads, bounded worker output, sanitized evidence, environment allowlisting, jailed model-only egress, and atomic receipt writes; no current security defect was verified.
Bash commands are recorded as successful task reads solely because their command text mentions task.ts, allowing unsupported read_calls and read_without_edit_attempts telemetry.
Checked batch execution and worker I/O: tasks are processed once, stream buffers and task reads are bounded, and receipts are checkpointed incrementally without an evident hot-path regression.
This test reads one fixed repository path and exercises local parser/cache functions; it has no auth, network, untrusted write, command, client, container, or RBAC surface.
Checked that the tests derive live session-column and persisted-envelope shapes, compare them with registered contracts, verify consumer version use, and keep distinct invalidation knobs separate.
This is a small release fence test, not shipped hot-path code or a new runtime surface.

findings.title: Command-name matching fabricates task-read telemetry
findings.what: commandMentionsTask() treats any Bash command containing the token task.ts as a read. isReadToolUse() accepts that predicate, and any non-error tool result increments read_calls. Consequently commands such as `echo task.ts` or `rm task.ts` produce evidence claiming a successful read and can also increment read_without_edit_attempts, although no input inspection occurred. The receipt therefore contains non-reproducible adherence telemetry.
findings.fix: Do not infer a read from a bare task.ts token. Count only a literal read tool targeting the task or explicitly recognized read/search operations whose structured target resolves to taskPath; otherwise mark Bash read evidence unknown rather than successful.
findings.acceptance: Add a focused toolTelemetry test proving a successful Bash `echo task.ts` event yields read_calls=0 and read_without_edit_attempts=0, while a recognized successful read of task.ts yields read_calls=1; also prove failed read results remain uncounted.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read the classifier and counter flow at scripts/model-eval-run.mjs:431-497 and the emitted telemetry mapping at lines 662-700. The predicate examines only token presence, not command semantics, so the counterexample deterministically survives without relying on external state.
